newsitem.title: JAPAN: Five arrested in Japan fraud scandal.
newsitem.headline: Five arrested in Japan fraud scandal.

text.p: Japanese police said they arrested five managers of an investment society on Monday in connection with a multi-billion yen fraud scandal.

Following the arrest of the five managers of Orange Kyosai Kumiai, police were also expected to seek an exemption from parliamentary immunity to arrest lawmaker Tatsuo Tomobe, Kyodo news agency quoted police sources as saying.
Tomobe's wife Mikiko, who heads the Orange group, and his son Momoo, were among the five arrested, police said.

The five managers are suspected of having illegally raised more than seven billion yen ($58.8 million) by offering a high-interest ''Orange Super Fund'' without any intention of investing the money, police said.

A significant amount of the fund was used to support the election campaigns of Tomobe, a member of the Upper House of parliament who quit the main opposition New Frontier Party last November when the scandal surfaced, media reports said.
He was questioned by police on Sunday at a Tokyo hospital where he has been admitted after suffering a stroke. Tomobe enjoys immunity from arrest while parliament is in session.
Lawmakers can be arrested during a parliamentary session if they are caught committing a crime or if the legislature gives permission.
